verdict.reasoning: Patient reports watery diarrhea: 'it's like... I think it's diarrhea... super watery... just pouring straight from my bum' and duration: 'it's been about three days now.'
Frequency: 'I feel like it's like almost every hour I'm awake.' Consistency and no blood: 'super watery' and 'No, I don't remember anything... There's nothing like that' when asked about blood.

Location: 'It's like at the bottom... in the middle to me. Not on any side.' Nature: 'I feel a cramp and then I know it's time to go.' Intermittent: 'It comes and goes.' Severity: 'maybe is that like a six or seven?'
'Yeah, I definitely feel kind of nauseous.'
'I have vomited... whenever I have, like, milk... I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah, one time I just... had some milk and I just completely vomited it.'
'I think I am pretty. I feel kind of really hot all the time... I haven't actually done any temperature reading or anything like that.'
'In terms of your water works? Are you passing urine? Okay?' 'Yeah, but I guess less frequently maybe, but it seems to be okay.'
'my brother has had, actually had something like this... he has it as well, for five days as well.'
'Are you keeping your fluids down?' 'So it just feels like the fluids do go down, but it just feels like it's going straight through.'
'When was the last time you had anything solid to eat?' 'So I had some... lunch today, but again, it just come out pretty loose.'
'it's been about three days now' referring to the onset of diarrhea.
'are you otherwise fitting well or do you have any other medical history?' Patient: 'Yeah, I think otherwise I'm fit. Well... I can't think of any related medical history... no, I don't think so.'
'I'll take it. You don't take any regular medications then?' Patient: 'No, I mean, I, I've been taking some, like, paracetamols and stuff like that lately.'
'I'll take it. You don't take any regular medications then?' Patient: 'No... I'm not on any regular medication or anything like that.'
'And do you have any allergies to any medications?' Patient: 'So I don't have any allergies that I know of.'
'My dad actually has colon cancer at the moment... he's sort of in his third stage.'
'Tell me more about your home situation. Who's at home with you?' Patient: 'I live with my um, sister and my mum.'
'So you mentioned work. What is it you do for work?' Patient: 'I work at an office in central London. It's... I work in government.'
'Do you smoke...?' Patient: 'So I smoke, I smoke for like socially but not like regularly. So normally if it's a Friday... I might have a cigarette.'

'So alcohol, you know, I might have a beer during the weekdays... Maybe on Fridays I have more alcohol... not every week but maybe once or twice a month that... I'll go out with my friends and we'll drink a lot.'

'How are things at home?... in general day to day life, are you managing okay?' Patient: 'it's been tricky going to work with all of this. I dislike taking time off work. I feel like I just want to go when I can. So I try and go.'
'I just haven't really... I don't normally actually eat with my family. I normally, I'm buying stuff and that kind of thing.'

Doctor: 'your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis.' History includes watery diarrhea for three days, lower midline cramps, nausea/vomiting, feeling hot, and brother with similar symptoms as documented earlier.
When asked about blood in stools, patient: 'No, I don't remember anything... There's nothing like that.'

Doctor: 'You're losing a lot of fluid there' and later: 'I am obviously worried about the fact that you are losing minerals and vitamins... if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.'
Doctor: 'you can get things like diurelite, which is a fluid replacement we can get from the pharmacy... You can just get over the counter.' and 'Make sure you drink plenty of fluids.'
Doctor: 'clear fluids you can use soft diet, things like soup, mash, and then gradually build up as much as your body can tolerate.'
Doctor: 'You can try just, you know, regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish.' Later: 'If you've got bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think paracetamol is very sensible.'
Doctor: 'Try and avoid alcohol if you can.'

Doctor: 'if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back because... if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.'
